name: Speed lines
summary: Three or more parallel horizontal bands in chrome or a raised moulding along a rounded body, so that a static object seems to move.
how: Run three to five bands parallel to the long axis of the body.
Space the bands 3 to 8mm apart and keep them the same length.
Wrap the bands round a curved end, so that they follow the radius of the body.

origin.note: Industrial designers apply the bands of aerodynamic trains and cars to radios, toasters and refrigerators.

adoptions.via: Raymond Loewy and his peers put chrome bands on household appliances and pencil sharpeners.
